TYRE RESPONSE / CORNERING BALANCE — IMPLEMENTATION WAVE

Exact gameplay baseline commit: c29e33d8f05f21d85c85a79947c51adcf0d67e50
Repository: iLuzionsX/Racing26

Goal: make the M5 grip limit progressive, readable, and controllable without blanket grip increases, arbitrary yaw damping, excessive smoothing, or hidden assists. Preserve the completed tyre-grip, steering-ratio, track-jitter, braking/suspension, low-speed-cornering, and high-speed-spinout work already present at this baseline.

Wave-1 evidence already gathered from eight read-only Muse Spark 1.3 xhigh agents. Important findings to treat as hypotheses requiring code-level verification:
- The steering input path is already speed-shaped for keyboard and preserves full analog rack; do not retune steering unless a falsifier fails.
- Surface friction has hard material boundaries, but that is not a sufficient explanation for on-road limit behavior; do not smooth track materials unless a dedicated boundary test proves it is the cause.
- TireModel currently computes pure longitudinal/lateral Magic-Formula forces, applies MF-style cross weighting, then a post-peak slideScale and a final superellipse projection. WheelDynamics relaxes slip and then force, with different lateral/longitudinal lengths.
- Avoid changing total peak grip as the primary fix. Focus on transition quality at combined-slip saturation/post-peak and transient recovery.
- Reference-load assignment must be verified from Vehicle/WheelDynamics/TireModel before proposing any fix; do not assume it is wrong.

IMPLEMENTATION WAVE: each agent may propose a patch. Keep it small, scoped, and testable. Do not apply hidden stability aids or global yaw damping. Do not alter unrelated UI/track code.

Agent assignments:
1) Tire-model implementer: inspect TireModel.ts + WheelDynamics.ts + m5G90.ts + tire tests. Propose the smallest physics change that makes the combined-slip/post-peak transition more progressive while preserving peak grip and steady-state capacity. Add/adjust deterministic tests that directly measure continuity and left/right symmetry.
2) Transient/balance implementer: independently inspect TireModel/WheelDynamics/Vehicle/Suspension/Differential and propose the smallest change, if any, needed for catchable modest slides and coherent brake/throttle/steer interaction. Prefer fixing state/relaxation coupling over damping the chassis. Add a falsifying regression test. If no change is justified, patch=null and say so.
3) Adversarial reviewer: inspect the same code and the existing test suite. Do not optimize for agreement. Identify failure modes in likely TireModel/WheelDynamics fixes, define before/after metrics, and propose only test/harness changes unless a clear production defect is proven.

Every report must include:
- exact branch/head inspected
- reproduction or deterministic test scenario
- code paths and mechanism
- before/after measurement expectation
- falsifier
- patch (unified diff) or patch=null
- tests to run
- risks / regressions to watch

Do not claim browser driving, tests, measurements, or runtime observations you did not actually perform.

Authorized configuration: Muse Spark 1.3 with reasoning.effort=xhigh.
